# msarima: Multi-Seasonal ARIMA Models

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

The **msarima** package provides tools for fitting, forecasting, and simulating ARIMA models with multiple seasonal components. It extends the standard ARIMA framework to handle time series with multiple seasonal patterns.

## Installation

You can install the development version of msarima from [GitHub](https://github.com/danigiro/msarima) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("danigiro/msarima")
```

Once available on [CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=msarima) (soon), you can install the released version with:

``` r
install.packages("msarima")
```

## Features

- **Maximum likelihood estimation**: Uses numerical optimization (BFGS) for parameter estimation
- **Forecasting**: Generate point forecasts and prediction intervals
- **Simulation**: Simulate from fitted models or directly from model specifications
- **Time series support**: Works with `msts` objects
- **Model diagnostics**: Standard errors, information criteria (AIC, BIC, AICc)

## Basic Usage

```{r example-fit}
library(msarima)

# Simulate data with two seasonal components (periods 7 and 30)
set.seed(123)
y <- msarima.sim(
  nsim = 500,
  order = c(1, 0, 1),
  seasonal = list(c(0, 0, 1), c(0, 0, 1)),
  seasonal.period = c(7, 30),
  ar = 0.6,
  ma = c(0.4, 0.3, 0.2),  # non-seasonal MA, seasonal MA1, seasonal MA2
  sigma2 = 0.5
)

# Fit the model
fit <- msarima(
  y,
  order = c(1, 0, 1),
  seasonal = list(c(0, 0, 1), c(0, 0, 1)),
  seasonal.period = c(7, 30)
)

# View results
summary(fit)
```

### Forecasting

```{r example-forecast}
# Generate forecasts
fc <- forecast(fit, h = 50)
plot(fc)
```

### Working with msts Objects

```{r example-ts}
y_msts <- msts(y, seasonal.periods = c(7, 30))
fit_msts <- msarima(
  y_msts,
  order = c(1, 0, 1),
  seasonal = list(c(0, 0, 1), c(0, 0, 1))
)
```
